Elena (People Ops): Quick policy note on travel across time zones and PTO conversion — short read, please RTFA.
Elena (People Ops): TL;DR: introduce a 24h Timezone Buffer for international work travel, an optional PTO conversion for travel recovery, and updated on-call recovery rules.
Elena (People Ops): Why: we saw multiple cases where teammates were expected to work immediately after long flights and this impacted wellbeing. New rules aim to standardize expectations and avoid surprise PTO usage.
Elena (People Ops): Rules summary: 1) Timezone Buffer: for flights crossing 6+ time zones or >8 hours flight time, employees are entitled to a 24 hour buffer where no meetings are required. 2) PTO conversion: employees can convert up to 2 buffer days into PTO if they want that time counted as PTO; manager approval required. 3) On-call recovery: if you were on-call during travel, you get 4 hours back as recovery time per day on-call, or alternative comp time with manager sign-off.
Maya: Does the buffer apply for short overnight trips?
Elena (People Ops): Short trips crossing fewer than 6 zones are not auto-buffered. Managers can grant a buffer case by case.
Jonah: Who books the buffer in calendar?
Elena (People Ops): The traveler or manager should block the buffer as "Travel Buffer" on the calendar and add the travel tag in the HR portal so People Ops sees it.
Carlos: How does this interact with client-facing SLAs? Some customers expect early demos the morning after arrival.
Elena (People Ops): If a customer commitment exists, the manager should negotiate with the customer or reassign the meeting. Exceptions are allowed if traveler agrees. We encourage rotating coverage to avoid forcing someone to work within the buffer.
HR Bot: Checklist: 1) Add travel details in HR portal within 3 days of booking. 2) Manager confirms buffer or exception. 3) If converting to PTO, submit PTO request before travel. Link: https://redwood-internal/hr/travel-buffer
Maya: Any payroll or benefits effect?
Elena (People Ops): No payroll changes. PTO conversion counts against your balance, recovery time is paid time and not deducted from PTO.
Jonah: Can contractors use buffer?
Elena (People Ops): Contractors do not get paid recovery time but managers can request comp time as a courtesy.
Elena (People Ops): We'll update the travel and PTO FAQ and run a 20-min drop-in next Tue. Ping me with edge cases. Thanks everyone.
